newsitem.title: UK: East Europe on the rise in firm Brady market.
newsitem.headline: East Europe on the rise in firm Brady market.

text.p: The brief correction in the surging emerging debt appears to have come to an end, with East European prices on Thursday picking up the lead from Latin America.

"The correction we saw up to yesterday lunchtime was less severe than I thought it would be," one European bank trader said, but added it was questionable whether the rally could resume at its recent pace.
However, after the market's pause for breath, investors are now waiting to see what happens to U.S. interest rates at next week's Federal Open Market Committee meeting.

Both Russian Vnesheokonombank debt and the when-and-if paper it will eventually turn into were higher in the morning, despite some arguments that prices were beginning to look a bit frothy after the past week's surge.
Vnesh dollar paper was trading around 70-1/4 to 70-3/8 cents in the dollar, close to recent all-time highs.
Bulgaria, largely shunned by the rest of the bull market, recovered some ground, largely on news that the government had finally agreed to privatise all its state banks, except for one.
The pledge is part of reforms the International Monetary Fund is demanding before it releases the delayed part of a loan.
However, analysts remain very cautious about the country's economic outlook which has mostly been seen as very bleak.
"It's still very precarious. The key issue for investors is that they can see better returns elsewhere," Deutsche Morgan Grenfell analyst Stuart Parkinson said.
It was questionable whether the risk/return made Bulgaria worthwhile for the investor, he added.
Argentina also managed to rise, helped by news that the lower house of Congress had approved the government's package to raise taxes, one trader said.
